title: Probing live KV instead of trusting stale telemetry
summary: A routing policy that asks the replica directly for its resident KV tokens, rather than reading a scrape that may be seconds old.

steps.title: A live probe instead of a scrape
body: This policy probes a replica's resident KV tokens directly at decision time, rather than routing on a periodic telemetry snapshot that finding 2 showed can be seconds stale.
The probe costs a modelled round trip per decision. That cost is visible in the routing latency panel rather than hidden.
steps.look_for: The per-decision probe latency tile, and the heatmap under Machine level staying comparatively flat.

steps.title: Load spread: CV 0.44 under 4 s staleness
body: Under a 4-second telemetry staleness setting, least_kv_probe holds a load-spread coefficient of variation of 0.44, against 0.63 for power-of-two-choices measured under the same staleness.
The probe sidesteps staleness by construction: it never reads the stale snapshot for the field that matters.
steps.look_for: The imbalance coefficient of variation tile reading noticeably lower than the p2c comparison quoted in the finding.

steps.title: What the probe is worth against p2c
body: p2c's 0.63 CV under 4 s staleness is a real number from the same U10 measurement, not a live comparison run in this walkthrough — there is no separate exported recording for p2c under matched staleness yet.
Use the Policies tab to switch this run's routing to power-of-two-choices live and watch the coefficient of variation move toward that 0.63 figure under the same staleness setting.
steps.look_for: The load-spread tile before and after switching the live policy.

steps.title: The cost side of the trade
body: A probe per decision is not free: it is a modelled RPC, visible in the routing-cost line rather than folded into general overhead.
Whether the balance improvement is worth that cost depends on how expensive the probe RPC is on the real system this is standing in for, which is a deployment question, not a simulation one.
steps.look_for: The routing-cost line in the Utilization tab, present here and absent for scrape-based policies.
